options: A substance that takes part in a chemical reaction — the starting material
The new substance a reaction creates
A type of element with no reactions
questions.explanation: A reactant is a starting material that takes part in and is consumed by a chemical reaction.
questions.misconception: The NEW substance is the product, not the reactant — the reactant is the material that goes INTO the reaction.

questions.prompt: Where are reactants written in a chemical equation?
options: On the LEFT side of the arrow
On the RIGHT side of the arrow
questions.explanation: Reactants are always written on the left of the arrow; products go on the right.
questions.misconception: The right side of the arrow belongs to the products — the left side is always the reactants.

questions.prompt: What happens to a reactant during a reaction?
options: It is consumed — its atoms are rearranged into the products
It disappears completely and the atoms vanish
questions.explanation: Reactants are used up, but their atoms are conserved — rearranged into the new substances on the right.
questions.misconception: Atoms are never destroyed in a chemical reaction — they are rearranged. The reactant's matter simply reappears, connected differently, in the products.

questions.prompt: In the reaction hydrogen + oxygen → water, which are the reactants?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen and oxygen are on the left — they are the reactants that combine to make the product, water.
questions.misconception: Water is the product, on the right — the reactants are the starting materials hydrogen and oxygen, both needed.
